name: Northern Army (Saratoga); Southern Army (Camden)
troop_source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battles_of_Saratoga : "the effective colonial force was about 12,000 men" (Saratoga, Oct 1777; Saratoga_campaign says "over 15,000" with militia). Southern Army: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Camden : "an American army of 4,000 regulars and militia under Major General Horatio Gates".

rows.label: Stillwater (assumes command of Northern Department army)
rows.quote: On August 19, Major General Horatio Gates assumed command from Schuyler
rows.note: Source places the army camp south of Stillwater near the Mohawk mouth; Stillwater is the nearest titled place. Gates article gives the same date; Congress had named him on Aug 4.

rows.label: Freeman's Farm (Saratoga)
rows.quote: assumed command himself of the right
rows.note: Gates directed the battle from the Bemis Heights fortifications (right wing), not Freeman's Farm itself. Event 19 also covers 1777-10-07.

rows.label: Bemis Heights (Saratoga)
rows.quote: assumed command of the American left
rows.note: Gates commanded from the Bemis Heights lines after relieving Arnold.

rows.label: Schuylerville (Burgoyne surrenders)
rows.quote: Burgoyne surrendered his army and tendered his sword to Gates
rows.note: Surrender site is about half a mile south of Schuylerville (Horatio_Gates article).

rows.label: Camden
rows.quote: Gates and staff stayed behind the reserve force

rows.label: Charlotte (flees after Camden, same evening)
rows.quote: had taken refuge 60 miles (97 km) away in Charlotte
rows.note: Same date as the battle; the source says he arrived by that evening.

rows.label: Hillsborough (reports defeat to Congress)
rows.quote: he arrived at Hillsborough on August 19
rows.note: Report to Congress written Aug 20 per same source.

rows.label: Newburgh army camp (Newburgh meeting of officers)
rows.quote: After Gates opened the meeting, Washington entered the building
rows.note: The Temple was at the army camp at New Windsor, by Newburgh; Newburgh is the place the article names.
